items.definition: talking about life experiences with hobbies and free time using the present perfect
items.explanationTR:
We use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about experiences in our life without saying exactly when they happened.

• Have you ever tried painting? — asking about a general experience.
• I have never gone hiking in the mountains. — an experience you have not had.
• She has tried many different hobbies this year. — experience up to now.

We often use 'ever' in questions and 'never' in negative sentences.
• Have you ever taken a cooking class?
• He has never been good at knitting.

When we know exactly when something happened, we use the past simple instead.
• I have visited that hiking trail. (an experience, no specific time)
• I visited that hiking trail last summer. (a specific time)

'Just', 'already', and 'yet' often appear with the present perfect: She has already tried gardening. Have you finished your painting yet?

Remember to use the past participle after have/has, not the past simple form (has gone, not has went). Common irregular participles: be → been, see → seen, take → taken, do → done. Use 'been' for places you visited and came back from: I have been to Japan.

questions.explanationTR: "Have" combines with "you" and the past participle to ask about a life experience; "Did" would need the past simple, and the other auxiliaries don't fit this structure.

questions.prompt: I ---- never been hiking in the mountains.
questions.explanationTR: The subject "I" takes "have" in the present perfect; "has" is for he/she/it, and the other options are not present perfect forms.

questions.prompt: She ---- tried many different hobbies this year.
questions.explanationTR: The subject "she" needs "has" in the present perfect; "have" is for I/you/we/they, and the other options are not present perfect.

questions.prompt: Have you ---- taken a cooking class before?
questions.explanationTR: "Ever" is used in present perfect questions asking about life experience; "yet" and "already" fit different kinds of sentences, and "never" is for negative statements.

questions.prompt: He has ---- been good at knitting; he always struggles with it.
questions.explanationTR: "Never" shows an experience that hasn't happened, matching "always struggles"; the other adverbs don't fit a negative experience.

questions.prompt: I ---- that hiking trail last summer.
questions.explanationTR: "Last summer" is a specific past time, so the past simple "visited" is correct; the present perfect options don't fit a stated specific time.

questions.prompt: She has already ---- her painting; you can see it now.
questions.explanationTR: After "has already", we need the past participle "finished"; the other forms do not complete the present perfect correctly.

questions.prompt: My brother loves hiking. He has ---- to the mountains in Nepal three times.
questions.explanationTR: "Been" is the past participle we use for visits and experiences ("has been to"); "went" is the past simple and can't follow "has", and "go", "being" and "was" are not past participles.

lessons.title: Reading: A hobby that changed my life

items.headword: A hobby that changed my life
items.definition: A short story about a hobby that changed someone's life, with seven questions

passage.title: A Hobby That Changed My Life
passage.body:
Five years ago, I was often stressed and bored after work. I didn't have any hobbies, and my free time felt empty. Then a colleague invited me to try hiking with her group on weekends.

At first, I wasn't very good at it. I felt nervous during the first trip because the trail was long and difficult. But I didn't give up. I kept practicing, and soon I started to enjoy the fresh air and the quiet mountains.

After a few months, I noticed a big change. I felt calmer and happier, even at work. I also made new friends in the hiking group, and we keep in touch every week. Hiking gave me something to look forward to, and it taught me to be more patient with myself.

Last year, I finally achieved a goal I never thought possible: I hiked to the top of a real mountain. I have never felt so proud. Now I encourage my friends to take up a hobby, too. It doesn't matter what hobby you choose — the important thing is to try something new and give it time. You might discover a talent you never knew you had.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel before starting hiking?
questions.explanationTR: The passage begins, "I was often stressed and bored after work," describing life before hiking; the other feelings are not mentioned for that time.

questions.prompt: Who invited the writer to try hiking?
questions.explanationTR: The passage says "a colleague invited me to try hiking with her group"; no family member, neighbor, classmate, or stranger is mentioned.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel during the first hiking trip?
questions.explanationTR: The writer says, "I felt nervous during the first trip because the trail was long and difficult"; the other feelings came later, not during the first trip.

questions.prompt: What changed after a few months of hiking?
options: The writer found a new job.
The writer moved to the mountains.
The writer felt calmer and happier.
The writer became a hiking guide.
questions.explanationTR: The passage says, "I felt calmer and happier, even at work"; the other changes are not mentioned in the passage.

questions.prompt: What did the writer achieve last year?
options: Hiking to the top of a mountain.
questions.explanationTR: The passage says the writer "hiked to the top of a real mountain" last year; the other achievements are not mentioned.

questions.prompt: What does the writer encourage friends to do?
questions.explanationTR: The writer says, "I encourage my friends to take up a hobby, too"; the other actions are not suggested in the passage.

questions.prompt: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Hiking is the best hobby for everyone.
Trying something new can change your life.
It's too hard to start a new hobby.
Only young people should try new hobbies.
Hobbies are not important for happiness.
questions.explanationTR: The passage's final lines encourage trying something new because it might reveal a hidden talent, showing that new experiences can change your life; the other statements contradict the passage's positive message.
